newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar ends down sharply on fund selling.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar ends down sharply on fund selling.

text.p: CSCE world sugar futures closed sharply lower after fund selling eroded nearby support and pressured benchmark October to a recent low, traders said.
Early selling triggered stops around 11.15 cents a lb and pushed the spot month to a midday low of 11.10 cents, where shortcovering by the trade and light local buying held the contract.

The selling eroded support in the afternoon and touched off stops below 11.10 cents, where the funds became more aggressive sellers. October fell to 11.03 cents, its lowest level since hitting 11.00 cents on June 23.
October settled 0.19 cent weaker at 11.05 cents, traded 11.26 to 11.03 cents. The rest ended 0.10 to 0.14 cent weaker.
The next downside target was seen at 11.00 to 10.96 cents followed by 10.80 cents in October.
"The key is what we do at 11.00 cents," Merrill Lynch sugar broker Tony Passimenti, said.
He noted trade shortcovering and buying on each point down by Far Eastern dealers around 11.05 cents in October.
"The next couple of points (lower) will be a real tug-of-war," he said.
Volume should remain thin on Thursday ahead of the Independence Day holiday. CSCE will be closed Friday in observance of U.S. Independence Day.
Prices are seen easing in the next week as the mounting open interest, which traders said reflects a heavy speculative net long position, could pressure the market.

As of early Tuesday, open interest in the most-active month rose by 3,573 lots to 98,363 lots. Open interest in second-position March, where brisk buying was cited on Tuesday, rose by 1,571 lots to 41,475 lots.
Firm resistance in October was pegged at its lifetime high of 11.40 cents, followed by 11.50 cents.
An estimated 24,933 lots changed hands on the day, compared with Tuesday's official 21,937 lots.
